tagline.text: Ayala's large shopping mall complex in Davao's Bajada district

location.label: Location
location.text: J.P. Laurel Avenue, Bajada, Davao City (Abreeza Ayala Business Park)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (especially good as a refuge from midday heat and rain)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱300~1,500 (meal, coffee and transport per person, excluding shopping)

children.text: Abreeza Mall opened in May 2011 and is a large shopping mall in downtown Davao, the first mall Ayala built in Mindanao. It sits in a mixed-use complex with a hotel, office building and residential towers, so shopping, meals and rest are all in one place.

Abreeza Mall is a four-story shopping mall on J.P. Laurel Avenue in Davao City's Bajada district. It opened on May 12, 2011, and is owned and operated by a joint venture between Ayala Land and the Anflo Group. As the first Ayala-brand mall in Mindanao, it is still the first place many Davao residents think of when they say "the Ayala mall." The mall occupies about 4 hectares of a roughly 10-hectare complex that also has an office building, residential towers and a hotel.

Inside you will find local and international fashion brands, a bookstore, homeware shops, restaurants and cafes, and sources describe the mall as having roughly 300 or more stores. It follows the classic Philippine mall layout, so first-time visitors will hardly ever get lost. It is well air-conditioned, which makes it a good place to escape the midday heat or a sudden downpour, and it also offers free Wi-Fi, customer lounges and a large car park. According to official information, parking capacity is about 1,200 cars.

The appeal of Abreeza as a travel stop is that it is the easiest way to see everyday Davao. It suits you whether you want to look for souvenirs such as durian candy, Davao chocolate or coffee, watch how Filipino families spend a weekend, or simply sort out your itinerary in cool, comfortable surroundings. It is connected to the hotel Seda Abreeza, and some reviews mention that hotel guests can walk to the mall through an indoor passage.

2026 marks the mall's 15th anniversary, and it is undergoing a major refresh. Work includes basement upgrades, new flooring and lighting, and improved common areas, along with a reshuffled tenant mix and a separate expansion wing costing about ₱2.5 billion. Depending on when you visit, some areas may be behind hoarding, so it helps to know this before you go. Reports say the new wing will have three retail levels and two office (BPO) floors with about
of leasable space, targeted to open in 2028. The existing mall remains open, but some stores may move or be partly boarded up, so check first if you are heading for a particular shop.

blocks.title: The first Ayala mall in Mindanao

children.text: Opened in 2011 as Ayala's first shopping mall in Mindanao. It is still regarded as one of the most refined shopping spaces in Davao and is visited by locals and foreign visitors alike.

With roughly 300 or more stores, you can browse clothing, shoes, books and home goods in one go. The 2026 refresh plans include new brand arrivals such as Hoka and Foot Locker's first Davao store, so check the mall's announcements for the latest tenant list.

A wide choice of Japanese food, fast food and coffee chains makes it easy to find something at every mealtime. The refresh plans include Kantinas, an air-conditioned food hall gathering brands from Davao, Cebu and other regions.
Seda Abreeza in the same complex is a 12-story, 186-room hotel owned by Ayala Land. Staying there puts the mall right next door, so you can shop and eat in the evening and head straight back.

blocks.title: Indoor relief from heat and rain

children.text: Davao is warm all year, so cool indoor space is welcome at midday. A cafe is a good place to rest, plan your day or recharge your devices.
Robinsons Department Store and Supermarket is an anchor tenant, which is handy for grocery shopping and everyday supplies. Check on site whether individual stores are open.
Within walking distance are a university, other shopping malls, the Davao Butterfly House and a local-history museum, making the mall a good base for continuing a city tour.
Arrive at the mall and get a feel for the floor layout from the ground-floor information desk and directory. Since it is the hottest part of the day, start with a cold drink at a cafe.
Browse the bookstore, home goods shops and fashion stores at a relaxed pace. Check in person whether the mall has stores selling Davao food products for souvenirs.
The mall starts to fill up when people leave work, so finish your grocery shopping before then.
Have dinner in the dining area. Choose a place that suits you, whether Filipino or Japanese food.
Call a taxi or Grab before closing time and head back to your hotel.

Have breakfast at your hotel and head to the Bajada district.
When the mall opens, spend time in a cafe or look around for things you want to buy in advance.

This plan covers about half a day. Even if places are close on foot, the midday sun is strong, so bring a hat and water and mix walking with taxi or Grab rides. Check each place's opening hours and admission just before you go.

Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines (PAL) fly nonstop from Manila (NAIA) to Davao International Airport (DVO); PAL Express may also operate some flights depending on the season, so check when booking. The flight takes about
2 hours
, and schedules and fares vary a lot by season, so check when booking.
Davao International Airport is in the Sasa district, north of the city center.
A taxi from the airport to Abreeza is generally cited at around
. It varies with time of day and traffic, so ask the driver to use the meter.
Ride-hailing taxis such as Grab are also available around the airport. If you have a lot of luggage, a taxi or Grab is the easiest option.

To travel cheaply, you can walk out to Diversion Road in front of the airport, take a jeepney marked "Panacan via Buhangin" and get off in the Bajada area. Fares and routes can change, so confirm with the driver.
From the city center it is a short taxi or Grab ride. Many jeepneys also run along J.P. Laurel Avenue in Bajada.
When calling a ride, specify the pickup or drop-off point clearly, such as "Abreeza Mall main entrance." Locations may change because of construction, so check the app's instructions.
Short distances can be covered on foot, but take the midday heat and road crossings into account.
Abreeza is an indoor mall, so it is barely affected by the seasons and can be visited year-round. It is especially valuable as a place to rest in the hot midday or when a downpour hits.

Crowd levels vary a lot by time of day. Weekday mornings and early afternoons are relatively quiet, while weekends, evenings after work, the year-end holidays and sale periods are busy. In December, Christmas decorations and sales make it especially crowded.

The most convenient place to stay is Seda Abreeza, which is connected to the mall. It is 12 stories with 186 rooms, and the mall is right next door, so getting around after shopping or dinner is short. Room rates vary with season and exchange rates, so check by date on a booking site. The Bajada district also has several other hotels and serviced apartments.

You can easily eat all your meals inside the mall. There are Japanese restaurants, fast food, coffee chains and Filipino home cooking, and The Dining Hall, the restaurant at Seda Abreeza, is rated highly on travel review sites. The 2026 refresh plans include Kantinas, an air-conditioned food hall of brands from Davao, Cebu and other regions, so check before you go whether it has opened.

Outside the mall, other shopping malls and restaurants in Bajada are within walking distance. Rather than spending a long time in one place, plan your day so that you rest at Abreeza and alternate with other areas. If you have a food allergy or follow a specific diet, check menus in advance and ask staff about ingredients at local restaurants. Cards are accepted at most places, but some small shops take cash only, so carry a little cash.

On hot days, bring a thin layer over a short-sleeved top. The air conditioning inside is quite strong.
Bag checks may be in place, so follow the staff's instructions at the entrance.
When taking a taxi or Grab, say "Abreeza Mall" as your destination and tell the driver whether you want to be dropped at the main entrance or the hotel entrance.
Traffic around Bajada is heavy during rush hour (5–7 p.m.), so allow extra travel time.
Construction for the 2026 refresh may block some areas. If there is a particular store you want to visit, check before you go.
If you are shopping for Davao specialties such as durian candy, compare prices with other shops in the city.
An expansion wing and refresh are underway, so parts of the mall and surrounding roads may be blocked. Check the latest announcements.
There have been reports of temporary road closures because of construction, so confirm your pickup and drop-off point in advance when calling a taxi.
The mall is relatively safe, but watch for pickpockets and lost phones in crowded areas.
In an emergency such as an earthquake, follow staff instructions and the exit signs. During the 2025 Davao Oriental earthquakes, some ceiling tiles reportedly fell inside the mall.
Opening hours, cinema operation and tenant lineups change often. Check just before you go.
Always ask the driver to use the meter, and consider Grab if you have a lot of luggage.
Abreeza is in the Bajada district of Davao City. City sightseeing is easy to continue from about
10–20 minutes
away by taxi.
A representative church in downtown Davao. It is an easy trip from the mall by taxi or Grab.
An island off the coast of Davao, best planned as a separate day trip after you finish shopping at the mall.
A mountain park away from the city, good for a trip when you want cooler weather. Check travel times locally.
